6-second continuous live-action historical epic shot, full-frame landscape 16:9. Reference image 1 defines the same Yiling camp, exact initial composition and LATE EVENING AFTER SUNSET lighting. Dark indigo sky, only a dim residual dusk band, no sun or daylight. Huge fierce fires illuminate nearby canvas and wood locally; faint cool skylight preserves necessary shadow detail. Maintain this evening exposure throughout this shot; do not brighten into daytime.
From 0 to 6 seconds the camera makes ONE restrained rightward lateral move along the earthen slope, with actual parallax between foreground broken cart and distant camp terraces. No zoom, no aerial rise, no orbit. The wide framing stays wide. Fires flutter strongly on already-burning tent roofs, separate smoke plumes rise, a few embers originate at the flames. Do not make every tent collapse simultaneously. Road bend, dead tree, watchtower and mountain notch remain coherent in perspective. Fire remains vigorous at the end. No added people. Dry scorched ground, textured real fabric, splintered wood and rope, readable foreground and middle distance. No rain, puddles, fog veil, fake CG, text or subtitles.

Audio: ONLY natural environmental and nonverbal action sound. Burning wood crackles and roars at appropriate distance; for soldiers, dry footsteps, clothes rubbing, restrained breathing and wooden wheels creaking follow actual movement. NO speech, NO narration, NO shouted words, NO singing, NO music, NO instruments, NO dramatic soundtrack or rhythmic drums. No engines or modern machinery. Do not read instructions aloud.
